## Jargon glosses (79)

Use the gloss once, on first use, then use the term freely.

| Term | Gloss |
|---|---|
| API | the way one program asks another for something |
| CD | a robot that ships every change that passes tests |
| CDN | servers near the user that hold copies of your files |
| CI | a robot that builds and tests every change |
| CORS | the browser rule about which sites can call which servers |
| CRUD | create, read, update, delete |
| DNS | the phone book that turns a domain into an address |
| ICP | ideal customer profile, the kind of buyer you actually want |
| JWT | a signed token that proves who you are |
| MCP | Model Context Protocol, the standard way tools plug into a model |
| OAuth | logging in through another service without sharing a password |
| ORM | code that talks to a database so you do not write SQL |
| RAG | looking things up before answering, so the model does not guess |
| SDK | a code kit for using someone else's service |
| SLA | a written promise about uptime, with a penalty |
| SLO | the internal target behind that promise |
| TLS | the encryption behind the padlock in the address bar |
| agent | a model that can take actions, not just reply |
| attention | how a model decides which words matter to each other |
| attribution | deciding which ad gets credit for a sale |
| backpressure | slowing the sender when the receiver is full |
| blue-green | two live copies, you flip traffic between them |
| burn | how fast the money leaves |
| cache invalidation | throwing away a saved copy that went stale |
| canary | shipping to a small slice of users first |
| churn | customers who leave |
| circuit breaker | stop calling a service that keeps failing |
| cohort | a group of users who signed up in the same period |
| container | an app packaged with everything it needs to run |
| context window | how much text a model can hold at once |
| conversion | a visitor doing the thing you wanted |
| deadlock | two jobs each waiting on the other, forever |
| declarative | you describe the end state, not the steps |
| distillation | training a small model to copy a big one |
| embedding | text turned into numbers so a computer can compare meaning |
| eventual consistency | everyone agrees, a moment later |
| feature flag | a switch that turns a feature on for some users |
| fine-tuning | retraining a model on your own examples |
| funnel | the steps between arriving and paying |
| hallucination | the model stating something false with confidence |
| idempotence | running it twice changes nothing |
| idempotency key | a token that stops a duplicate charge |
| idempotent | running it twice changes nothing |
| immutable | cannot be changed after it is made |
| imperative | you write the steps |
| inference | the model actually answering, as opposed to training |
| kubernetes | the system that runs and restarts containers for you |
| latency | how long a request takes |
| memoization | remembering an answer instead of recomputing it |
| microservices | many small applications talking to each other |
| middleware | code that runs between the request and the answer |
| migration | a scripted change to a database's shape |
| monolith | one big application |
| observability | being able to see what a live system is doing |
| orchestration | one system telling the others what to do next |
| p95 | the slowest 5% of requests, the number users complain about |
| polling | asking again and again until something changes |
| prompt injection | hidden text that hijacks an AI's instructions |
| quantization | shrinking a model by storing it less precisely |
| race condition | two things happening in the wrong order |
| rate limit | a cap on how often you can call something |
| refactor | rewriting code without changing what it does |
| regression | something that used to work and now does not |
| replication | keeping a second copy in sync |
| rollback | putting the previous version back |
| runway | how long the money lasts |
| schema | the shape data has to fit |
| serverless | you run code without managing the machine |
| sharding | splitting one database into several |
| system prompt | the standing instructions a model always sees |
| technical debt | shortcuts you will pay for later |
| telemetry | the numbers a running system reports about itself |
| temperature | how much randomness the model is allowed |
| throughput | how much work gets done per second |
| token | roughly three quarters of a word, the unit models are billed in |
| tool call | the model asking your code to do something |
| transformer | the model design behind almost all current AI |
| vector database | a store that finds text by meaning, not by keyword |
| webhook | one service calling your URL when something happens |
